relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It reports another case of holoprosencephaly with a RAD21 loss-of-function variant, which adds to the midline brain defect part of the CDLS4 phenotype.

findings.statement: Goel and Parasivam (2020) reported another case of holoprosencephaly associated with a loss-of-function variant in the RAD21 gene.
quotes: Another case of holoprosencephaly associated with RAD21 loss-of-function variant.

relevance_reason: Large case series of 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 variants or microdeletions. It defines the CdLS4 phenotype, compares it with NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts, models variant effects on the protein and reports genotype–phenotype findings.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations: 24 different intragenic sequence variants (2 of them recurrent) and 7 unique microdeletions. Twenty-four of the cases were previously unpublished. Full clinical information was available for 29 patients from 22 families (cohort A). Their phenotype was an attenuated form of CdLS compared with that caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, especially for facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition and behavior. Patients came from Australia, Europe, Turkey, Canada and the United States.
quotes: We gathered a series of 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations [24 different intragenic sequence variants (2 recurrent), 7 unique microdeletions], including 24 hitherto unpublished cases.
Their phenotype is an attenuated CdLS phenotype compared to that caused by variants in NIPBL or SMC1A for facial morphology, limb anomalies, and especially for cognition and behavior.
Patients originated from Australia, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, United Kingdom and United States.
findings.population: Australia, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, United Kingdom, United States

findings.statement: In cohort A (29 patients aged 0 to 61 years; 15 males), Krab et al. (2020) found that all patients had CdLS scores of at least 5. Common features included a short nose (23/26), a long and/or smooth philtrum (26/29), a concave nasal ridge (24/29), thick eyebrows (20/24), long eyelashes (21/26), synophrys (19/28), a short fifth finger (23/28) and postnatal microcephaly (16/28). No patient had a major limb malformation. Small hands (5/27), small feet (3/27), hirsutism (10/26), seizures (2/22) and visual impairment (0/24) were less frequent than in the NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts. Hearing loss occurred in 8 of 24 patients, heart anomalies in 9 of 23, gastroesophageal reflux in 13 of 25 and cleft palate in 6 of 25.
quotes: All patients in cohort A (age range 0–61 years, median 9 years, mean 18 years; 15 males) had CdLS scores of at least five, sufficient to warrant molecular genetic testing for CdLS.
RAD21 patients less frequently have increased body hair (hirsutism, bushy eyebrows, low scalp hair lines), major limb malformations are not reported, and hands and feet are generally of normal size.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found that cognition and behavior were attenuated in RAD21 patients compared with NIPBL and SMC1A patients. Of the 29 patients, 16 (55%) had normal cognition or mild intellectual disability, 4 had moderate disability and none had severe or profound disability. All patients aged 3 years or older used some words. Fourteen of 25 had behavioral problems, mainly anxiety, ADHD, autism spectrum disorder features and obsessive-compulsive behavior. Self-injurious behavior and aggression were each seen in only 1 patient.
quotes: The majority of RAD21 patients (16/29, 55%) have normal or mildly impaired cognitive functioning (SMC1A group 32%; NIPBL group 7%)
14/25 RAD21 patients (56%) with sufficiently available information on behavior had problems, mainly features of anxiety, ADHD, ASD, and obsessive–compulsive behavior.
Self-injurious behavior | 1/18 | 6 | 11/31 | 35 | 47/61 | 77

phenotypes.text: delay in one or more developmental milestones

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) summarized the natural history of RAD21-related CdLS. Pregnancy and birth usually progressed normally, and prenatal growth retardation was uncommon. About half of the patients had congenital anomalies such as cleft palate or cardiac anomalies. Diaphragmatic hernia, anal atresia and choanal atresia occurred occasionally. Short stature and microcephaly developed postnatally. Vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut were unusual findings that were relatively frequent in this series.
quotes: About half of the patients have congenital anomalies (cleft palate; cardiac anomalies). Major limb defects have not been found; diaphragmatic hernia, anal atresia or choanal atresia occur occasionally.
Unusual anomalies in the RAD21 cases are vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae).
Malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut are relatively frequent in RAD21 patients and have only rarely been described in CdLS

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) noted that the limited clinical information on cohort B suggested that biallelic RAD21 variants can cause Mungan syndrome and that monoallelic variants can cause holoprosencephaly, as in one cohort A case. They also suggested a possible link with schizophrenia but noted that this association may be coincidental. On follow-up, members of the family with Mungan syndrome showed CdLS characteristics that had not been mentioned in the original publication.
quotes: The (limited) available information of individuals from cohort B suggests that biallelic RAD21 variants can also lead to Mungan syndrome and monoallelic RAD21 variants to holoprosencephaly (like one case in cohort A) and possibly schizophrenia, although in the latter the association may be a spurious coincidence.

Indeed, when we succeeded in obtaining further clinical information, several individuals turned out to show CdLS characteristics not mentioned in the publication (for instance in the family with Mungan syndrome).

findings.statement: In 33 families, Krab et al. (2020) identified 31 different RAD21 alterations: 7 unique deletions (6 of which also included other genes) and 24 intragenic sequence variants. Of the sequence variants, 13 were predicted to be truncating (2 nonsense, 2 splice site and 9 frameshift) and were scattered throughout the gene, whereas missense variants tended to cluster in the functional domains. The variants were frequently familial (9 of 21 index cases in which inheritance could be determined).
quotes: The 33 families harbor 31 different variants: seven unique copy number variations (CNVs) and 24 intragenic sequence variants.
A relatively large proportion of the cases are familial (nine out of 21 index cases for whom inheritance could be established).
Of the 24 different sequence variants, 13 are predicted be truncating (2 nonsense, 2 splice site and 9 frameshift variants), and these are scattered throughout the gene.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found the recurrent heterozygous RAD21 missense variant c.1753T>C (p.Cys585Arg) in 2 families. It arose de novo in 1 patient and was present in 2 relatives of another family whose parents were not tested. Molecular dynamics modeling predicted that Cys585Arg causes the adjacent Arg586 to lose its salt bridge with Glu577, destabilizing the RAD21-SMC1A domain.
quotes: F13 | Deardorff 2012, P6 | Orginal data | ≥ 12 | Exon 14 | c.1753T > C | p.(Cys585Arg) | Missenseb | De novo
Cys585Arg has a similar effect, interacting with Glu583 and causing Arg586 to lose its contact with Glu577.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found the recurrent heterozygous RAD21 nonsense variant c.1756C>T (p.Arg586*) in 2 families. In one of them it was inherited from an affected father. Facial morphology varied between the families carrying this variant.
quotes: F16a | Unpublished | New | 10 | Exon 14 | c.1756C > T | p.(Arg586*) | Nonsense | Familial (paternal)
Interfamilial variability is illustrated by the comparison of facial morphology between patients F15 and F16a/b who harbor the p.(Arg586*) variant.

findings.statement: In a multigenerational family previously reported by Boyle et al. (2017), Krab et al. (2020) updated the data on 5 members who carried the heterozygous RAD21 frameshift variant c.704delG (p.Ser235Ilefs*19). Facial morphology varied within the family.
quotes: F6a | Boyle 2017 IV.16 | Updated | 12 | Exon 7 | c.704delG | p.(Ser235Ilefs*19) | Frameshift | Familial (maternal)
Intrafamilial variability is illustrated by the comparison of facial morphology between the members of family F6 and of family F16.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported a patient with a de novo RAD21 in-frame deletion, c.1774_1776del (p.Gln592del), and an unrelated patient with c.1800_1802del (p.Phe600del). Molecular dynamics modeling predicted that Gln592del moves Lys605 and so disturbs the positioning of SMC1A Asn35 at ATPase site 1. Phe600del did not affect RAD21 structure in the model, but the authors considered it likely pathogenic because the patient had classic CdLS and no variants in other known CdLS genes.
quotes: F17 | Gudmunsson 2019 | Updated | 8 | Exon 14 | c.1774_1776del | p.(Gln592del) | Inframe deletionb | De novo

Although the Phe600del variant does not seem to affect RAD21 structure, it leads to a classical CdLS phenotype without variants in additional known CdLS genes (using a targeted gene panel). Thus, it does seem likely pathogenic.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported a patient with a de novo RAD21 missense variant, c.1808T>C (p.Leu603Pro). Modeling predicted that Pro603 changes the bending angle of the alpha helix and moves Lys605 away from ATPase site 1.
quotes: F29 | Lee 2014 P76 | Original data | | Exon 14 | c.1808T > C | p.(Leu603Pro) | Missenseb | De novo

Presence of mutated Pro603 instead of wild-type Leu603 promotes a local change in the bending angle of the alpha-helix in which it is located, resulting in a conformational change in the alpha helix that moves Lys605 out of its initial position close to ATPase site 1

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported a patient with a de novo RAD21 missense variant in the STAG-binding domain, c.1033T>C (p.Ser345Pro). Modeling predicted that it impairs the RAD21–STAG1/2 interaction by inducing a new curved alpha-helix segment that pulls away from the STAG2 surface. In a previously reported patient, the de novo variant c.1127C>G (p.Pro376Arg) was predicted to form a new salt bridge with STAG2, over-stabilizing the interaction between the two proteins.
quotes: F26 | Decipher 275402 | New | | Exon 9 | c.1033T > C | p.(Ser345Pro) | Missenseb | De novo

The Ser345Pro variant impairs RAD21 and STAG1/2 interactions due to promotion of a de novo curved small alpha-helix segment that binds to the pre-existing alpha helix, which separates from the surface of STAG2.
Nevertheless, Pro376Arg does promote the formation of a new salt bridge between RAD21 and STAG2, which is predicted to cause over-stabilization of the interaction between the two proteins.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) updated the data on the family with Mungan syndrome reported by Bonora et al. (2015), in which 3 affected sibs were homozygous for the RAD21 variant c.1864G>A (p.Ala622Thr). Three further family members were heterozygous and had some clinical features of the CdLS spectrum. However, it remained uncertain whether they had a full CdLS phenotype or whether the variant causes disease in the heterozygous state. Modeling showed no structural change from Ala622Thr, but the authors noted that Ala622 lies next to Thr623, a PLK1 phosphorylation site.
quotes: F30a | Bonora 2015 IV.9 | Updated | | Exon 14 | c.[1864G > A];[1864G > A] | p.(Ala622Thr) | Missenseb | Familial (both parents)

The heterozygous members of this family had some clinical features of the CdLS spectrum, but as it was not possible to retrieve further clinical data, it remains uncertain whether they have a full CdLS phenotype, and whether this variant can lead to a phenotype in heterozygous form.

phenotypes.text: Mungan syndrome with chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) considered several other modeled or unmodeled RAD21 variants to be likely pathogenic. These were Arg65Gln (c.194G>A), which lies near the Arg-X-Tyr kinase/phosphatase recognition motif around Tyr67; Phe6Val (c.16T>G, de novo), which lies near the phosphorylation site Ser9; and Thr461Ile (c.1382C>T, inherited from the father), which is flanked by serines involved in phosphorylation-regulated release of cohesin from chromosome arms.
quotes: If phenotype data and literature/database information are taken into account, three more RAD21 modeled missense variants are likely pathogenic (Arg65Gln (reported as VUS), Phe600del, Ala622Thr).
The Phe6Val variant (reported as aVUS) would modify the kinase/phosphatase recognition motif, thus affecting the protein behavior.
F10 | Unpublished | New | 10 | Exon 11 | c.1382C > T | p.(Thr461Ile) | Missense | Familial (paternal)

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported a mother and child (family F11) carrying a 665-bp in-frame deletion in RAD21, c.1621-388_1704+193del (p.Asp541_Gln568del), which removes all of exon 13. The child inherited the deletion from the mother.
quotes: F11a | Minor 2014 P1 | Updated | 8 | Exon 13 | c.1621-388_1704 + 193del | p.(Asp541_Gln568del) | Inframe deletion | Familial (maternal)
Three of the variants are in-frame deletions, two of which affect a single amino acid, while the 665 bp deletion includes the whole exon 13.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) identified 7 deletions that included RAD21. Six also removed neighboring genes; one was a 27-kb deletion confined to RAD21 exons 1–9 (8q24.11). Patients with microdeletions tended to have higher CdLS scores and more frequent growth impairment than those with intragenic variants, but the frequency of major malformations and of cognitive and behavioral problems did not differ. Exostoses related to EXT1 haploinsufficiency likely caused upper limb anomalies in some patients with deletions.
quotes: The seven CNVs were all deletions, six of which included other genes in addition to RAD21.
F22 | Unpublished | New | 12 | Exons 1–9 | arr[hg19] 8q24.11(117866471–117893495)x1 | 27 kb deletion |

There was a trend towards higher CdLS scores and more frequently impaired growth parameters in patients with microdeletions compared to those with intragenic variants, but no differences were apparent in frequency of major malformations or cognitive and behavioral problems.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found no difference in CdLS scores or growth parameters between patients with truncating and those with non-truncating RAD21 sequence variants. In 12 of 15 patients with intragenic variants and major malformations or health problems, the variant lay in a protein-binding domain, but the authors noted that it was uncertain whether this was a true association. Variability within and between families was striking, especially for cognition and behavior, and could not be explained by mosaicism in most families.
quotes: There was no difference in CdLS scores or growth parameters between individuals with truncating and those with non-truncating sequence variants (median 10; range 9–13 and median 9.5; range 5–12, respectively).
For 12/15 patients with intragenic variants and major malformations or health problems, the variant was located in a protein-binding domain
The intrafamilial variation can be considerable (Tables S1, S3-4; Fig. 3), especially in cognition and behavior.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) suggested that the relatively mild phenotype indicates that RAD21 is not highly intolerant to loss of function, unlike other CdLS genes. They speculated that RAD21 haploinsufficiency may be compensated more effectively than that of other cohesin genes. However, patients with microdeletions or truncating variants did not differ markedly from those with missense variants. Modeling suggested that pathogenic variants in the SMC1A-binding domain disturb the ATPase reaction that is pivotal to opening of the cohesin ring.
quotes: The relatively mild phenotype of patients with RAD21 variants seems to indicate that RAD21 is not highly intolerant to loss-of-function, in contrast to other CdLS-associated genes (NIPBL, SMC1A, PDS5, WAPL, STAG2)

However, patients with haploinsufficiency for RAD21 due to microdeletions or truncating variants do not differ markedly from those with missense variants, and nonsense-mediated decay is not apparent although in the present series of patients this was not formally tested.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found that applying the CdLS consensus criteria for molecular testing would not have missed any RAD21 variant, and concluded that the CdLS score remains a reliable tool. CdLS was suspected before testing in 13 of 21 index cases. Because familial occurrence was frequent and variability within families was marked, the authors recommended testing parents even when they appear unaffected.
quotes: No RAD21 variant would have been missed using the CdLS consensus criteria for molecular studies (Kline et al. 2018).
Parental testing is warranted, even if signs or symptoms are apparently absent in parents, and standard testing of parents may further broaden the phenotype of RAD21 variants.

relevance_reason: The abstract reports holoprosencephaly in people with cohesin gene variants, including RAD21 (the CDLS4 gene). This supports the midline brain defect part of the phenotype. However, the abstract gives no RAD21 variant details and no count of RAD21 cases on their own.

findings.statement: Kruszka et al. (2019) reported holoprosencephaly in 4 individuals with variants in the non-X-linked cohesin complex genes SMC3 and RAD21. They also reported holoprosencephaly in 11 individuals with variants in the X-linked cohesin genes STAG2 and SMC1A: 10 had loss-of-function variants and 1 had a missense variant.
quotes: Additionally, we report four individuals with variants in the cohesin complex genes that are not X-linked, SMC3 and RAD21.
Here we report holoprosencephaly associated with variants in the two X-linked cohesin complex genes, STAG2 and SMC1A, with loss-of-function variants in 10 individuals and a missense variant in one.

findings.statement: Kruszka et al. (2019) concluded that the cohesin complex is an important regulator of median forebrain development. In human neural stem cells, shRNA knockdown of STAG2 and SMC1A caused aberrant expression of the holoprosencephaly-associated genes ZIC2, GLI2, SMAD3, and FGFR1.
quotes: we found that shRNA knockdown of STAG2 and SMC1A causes aberrant expression of HPE-associated genes ZIC2, GLI2, SMAD3 and FGFR1 in human neural stem cells.
These findings show the cohesin complex as an important regulator of median forebrain development and X-linked inheritance patterns in holoprosencephaly.

relevance_reason: Case report of a new patient with a novel RAD21 mutation and mild CdLS, adding to the phenotype delineation of CDLS4. Only the abstract was available, and it gives no variant details.

findings.statement: Dorval et al. (2020) reported a boy with a mild presentation of Cornelia de Lange syndrome and a molecularly confirmed novel RAD21 mutation. They compared his clinical features with those of previously reported patients who carried other RAD21 intragenic mutations. The authors noted that RAD21 is associated with a milder phenotype and that very few RAD21 intragenic mutations had been identified.
quotes: A novel RAD21 mutation in a boy with mild Cornelia de Lange presentation: Further delineation of the phenotype.
We discuss a new patient with RAD21 confirmed molecular diagnosis and compare his clinical features to those of previously described patients carrying different RAD21 intragenic mutations.
Among them, RAD21 is associated with a milder phenotype. Very few RAD21 intragenic mutations have been identified so far.

relevance_reason: Reports a new CdLS4 patient with a de novo RAD21 in-frame deletion and in silico structural modeling.

findings.statement: Gudmundsson et al. (2019) reported a 15-month-old boy with Cornelia de Lange syndrome type 4 who had developmental delay, distinct CdLS-like facial features, gastrointestinal reflux in early infancy, testis retention, prominent digit pads, and diaphragmatic hernia. The authors stated that the patient expanded the clinical description of CdLS4.
quotes: We report a 15-month-old boy presenting with developmental delay, distinct CdLS-like facial features, gastrointestinal reflux in early infancy, testis retention, prominent digit pads and diaphragmatic hernia.
In conclusion, we report a patient that expands the clinical description of CdLS type 4

findings.statement: In a boy with CdLS4, Gudmundsson et al. (2019) used exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous 3-bp deletion in the RAD21 gene (c.1774_1776del), resulting in an in-frame deletion of glutamine-592 (p.Gln592del). The variant was absent from both healthy parents and was predicted to be disease-causing by bioinformatic analysis. In silico structural modeling predicted that the deletion disrupts contact between RAD21 lys591 and SMC1A residues glu1191 and glu1192, changing the RAD21-SMC1A interface.
quotes: Exome sequencing revealed a novel RAD21 variant, c.1774_1776del, p.(Gln592del), suggestive of CdLS type 4.
Segregation analysis of the two healthy parents confirmed the variant as de novo and bioinformatic analysis predicted the variant as disease-causing.

Assessment by in silico structural model predicted that the p.Gln592del variant results in a discontinued contact between RAD21-Lys591 and the SMC1A residues Glu1191 and Glu1192, causing changes in the RAD21-SMC1A interface.

relevance_reason: Reports a novel RAD21 frameshift variant in a family with CdLS and shows intrafamilial phenotypic variability and incomplete penetrance.

findings.statement: In a patient with mild Cornelia de Lange syndrome, Boyle et al. (2017) identified a novel single-basepair deletion in the RAD21 gene (c.704delG). The deletion was predicted to cause a frameshift resulting in a premature stop codon (p.Ser235IlefsTer19), and the authors predicted it to be deleterious. The deletion was also present in the patient's mother and two aunts.
quotes: In a patient with CdLS (IV.16) we identifed a novel single basepair deletion (c.704delG) in RAD21, which encodes a cohesin pathway protein.
The variant is predicted to result in a premature stop codon [p.(Ser235Ilefs*19)] and hereby would have a deleterious effect.
Notably, the deletion was found in the mother and the two aunts of the index patient

findings.statement: Boyle et al. (2017) described a family with intrafamilial phenotypic variation associated with a RAD21 deletion. The index patient was classified as having mild Cornelia de Lange syndrome. The patient's mother and two aunts, who also carried the deletion, did not meet the diagnostic criteria for CdLS, and none of them had been suspected of having CdLS or a cohesinopathy before this study.
quotes: The index patient can be classified as mild CdLS, but the other family members do not fulfill the diagnostic criteria of CdLS.
none of them had been suspected of having CdLS or a cohesinopathy prior to this study

findings.statement: Boyle et al. (2017) suggested that, based on their study and previous reports, RAD21 variants are associated with incomplete penetrance and that carriers may therefore be underdiagnosed. They noted that RAD21 variants had previously been described in only 5 patients with cohesinopathies.
quotes: This study together with previous reports suggests incomplete penetrance associated with RAD21 variants and these individuals may therefore be underdiagnosed.
RAD21 variants have previously been described only in five cases with cohesinopathies

relevance_reason: Reports two patients with atypical/mild CdLS carrying novel RAD21 mutations (intragenic exon 13 deletion inherited from mother; c.592_593dup frameshift), directly relevant to CDLS4.

findings.statement: Minor et al. (2014) reported 2 patients with atypical, mild Cornelia de Lange syndrome-like presentation carrying RAD21 mutations. The first patient had developmental delay, hypospadias, inguinal hernia, and dysmorphic features; the second had developmental delay, characteristic facial features, hirsutism, and hand and feet anomalies, with the first patient being milder than the second.
quotes: The first patient presented with developmental delay, hypospadias, inguinal hernia and dysmorphic features while, the second patient presented with developmental delay, characteristic facial features, hirsutism, and hand and feet anomalies, with the first patient being milder than the second.

findings.statement: In a patient with mild atypical CdLS, Minor et al. (2014) identified an in-frame intragenic deletion of exon 13 of the RAD21 gene, the first intragenic deletion reported in RAD21. The deletion was inherited from the mother, who had a history of melanoma and other unspecified medical problems; this was described as the first familial case, and the authors discussed variable clinical presentation within families and low penetrance.
quotes: One patient had an in-frame deletion of exon 13, while the second patient had a c.592_593dup frameshift mutation.
The in-frame deletion mutation was found to be inherited from the mother who had a history of melanoma and other unspecified medical problems.
the variability of clinical presentation within families and low penetrance of mutations

findings.statement: In a patient with atypical CdLS including developmental delay, characteristic facial features, hirsutism, and hand and feet anomalies, Minor et al. (2014) identified a c.592_593dup frameshift mutation in the RAD21 gene.
quotes: One patient had an in-frame deletion of exon 13, while the second patient had a c.592_593dup frameshift mutation.
We report the first intragenic deletion and frameshift mutations identified in RAD21 in two patients presenting with atypical CdLS.

relevance_reason: This is the original report showing that RAD21 mutations cause a cohesinopathy with CdLS-like features, which is the CDLS4 phenotype.

findings.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) reported that children with RAD21 mutations had growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features overlapping those of Cornelia de Lange syndrome. Unlike individuals with NIPBL, SMC1A, or SMC3 mutations, they had much milder cognitive impairment than is seen in classical CdLS.
quotes: Children with RAD21 mutations display growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features that overlap findings in individuals with CdLS.
Notably, unlike children with mutations in NIPBL, SMC1A, or SMC3, these individuals have much milder cognitive impairment than those with classical CdLS.

findings.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) identified mutations in RAD21, which encodes an integral structural protein of the cohesin complex, in children with a congenital cohesinopathy phenotype. The mutations acted at the interface of RAD21 with the cohesin proteins STAG2 and SMC1A.
quotes: Here we show that human mutations in the integral cohesin structural protein RAD21 result in a congenital phenotype consistent with a "cohesinopathy."
Mechanistically, these mutations act at the RAD21 interface with the other cohesin proteins STAG2 and SMC1A

findings.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) found that the RAD21 mutations impaired the cellular DNA damage response and disrupted transcription in a zebrafish model.
quotes: impair cellular DNA damage response, and disrupt transcription in a zebrafish model

findings.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) suggested that dominant missense mutations in RAD21 cause more severe functional defects than loss-of-function mutations, and lead to worse structural and cognitive clinical findings.
quotes: Our data suggest that, compared to loss-of-function mutations, dominant missense mutations result in more severe functional defects and cause worse structural and cognitive clinical findings.

relevance_reason: The abstract describes a boy with a small 8q24.1 microdeletion that the authors say involves EXT1 alone, with a Langer-Giedion-like phenotype. It does not mention RAD21 or Cornelia de Lange features, so on its own it gives only cytogenetic context for this entry.

findings.statement: McBrien et al. (2008) reported a boy with a small 8q24.1 microdeletion, characterized by oligo array CGH, that involved EXT1 alone and not TRPS1. He had a mild Langer-Giedion-like phenotype. The authors suggested that this pointed to a functional disturbance of TRPS1. He also had unusual features, including prominent toe pads and fat pads on the soles of his feet, similar to those described in Pierpont syndrome.
quotes: We report on a boy with an oligo array-cgh characterized small microdeletion involving EXT1 alone but with some features of Langer-Giedion syndrome suggesting a functional disturbance of TRPS1.

This boy, in addition to a mild Langer-Giedion like phenotype, also had some unusual features including prominent toe pads and fat pads on the soles of his feet similar to those described in Pierpont syndrome.

phenotypes.text: fat pads on the soles of the feet

relevance_reason: The abstract describes a boy with a de novo 8q24 interstitial deletion that includes EXT1 and genes distal to it, with multiple exostoses, hypertrichosis, mental retardation and epilepsy. It is useful context for 8q24 contiguous gene deletions, but the abstract does not name RAD21 or Cornelia de Lange syndrome.

findings.statement: Wuyts et al. (2002) described a boy with multiple exostoses, hypertrichosis, mental retardation, epilepsy, and brain abnormalities.
quotes: Here we describe a boy with multiple exostoses, hypertrichosis, mental retardation, and epilepsy due to a de novo deletion on chromosome 8q24.

findings.statement: In a boy with multiple exostoses, hypertrichosis, mental retardation, and epilepsy, Wuyts et al. (2002) identified a de novo submicroscopic interstitial deletion of chromosome 8q24. On molecular analysis, the deletion overlapped the Langer-Giedion syndrome region and included the EXT1 gene and additional genes distal to EXT1. The authors concluded that it probably did not include the TRPS1 gene, which lies proximal to EXT1.
quotes: Molecular analysis revealed that the deletion interval overlaps with the Langer-Giedion syndrome and involves the EXT1 gene and additional genes located distal to EXT1, but probably not encompassing the TRPS1 gene located proximal to EXT1.
due to a de novo deletion on chromosome 8q24
